A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LAW and retain identifiable methods and experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original nuScenes and CARLA experiments, component ablations, and appendix analyses of view selection and runtime.

after.justification: v2 retains original driving experiments and adds NAVSIM results, perception-based experiments, and appendix studies of multi-step prediction and multiple input frames.

M1.justification: v2 removes v1's reward-based view-selection and latent-substitution branch. It introduces a perception-based BEV encoder and decoder with motion-prediction and map-construction losses, using deformable attention for latent prediction. Appendix A.1 also introduces autoregressive prediction and multiple input frames. Action-conditioned latent forecasting remains the central method.

E1.justification: v2 adds NAVSIM using OpenScene/nuPlan driving logs resampled to reduce simple scenarios, alongside the retained nuScenes and CARLA Town05 Long benchmarks. Its new perception-based framework also trains motion-prediction and map-construction tasks, substantially broadening the evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: BEV-Planner joins the nuScenes comparison. The new NAVSIM comparison includes Constant Velocity, Ego Status MLP, TransFuser, UniAD and PARA-Drive, with a human reference, adding substantially different comparators rather than simply transferring the previous comparator set. The CARLA comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include NAVSIM's PDMS and component metrics with a 20-epoch ResNet-34 setup, 48+12-epoch training for the BEV framework, and front-camera temporal experiments with 12+6-epoch training. Runtime comparisons disappear. v2 Table 1 explicitly distinguishes BEV-Planner's collision calculation from that used for other rows; this does not establish a change to LAW's retained collision metric.

E4.justification: v2 adds perception-based and NAVSIM latent-prediction ablations, a 10-second prediction horizon, autoregressive and multiple-input-frame studies, and qualitative comparisons with VAD. It removes the no-temporal-aggregation control and the view-selection, front-camera, fixed-versus-dynamic selection and latency analyses. The existing architecture and CARLA ablations are retained, although relocated or combined.

E5.justification: The CARLA comparisons and ablations retain the same plus/minus reporting. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added nuScenes and NAVSIM results use point estimates without introducing a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained headline results match: perception-free nuScenes averages remain 0.61 m L2 and 0.30% collision, and CARLA driving score remains 70.1 ± 2.6. v2 adds perception-based nuScenes results of 0.49 m and 0.19%, NAVSIM PDMS of 84.6, and new temporal-study results, while removing selection and runtime results. These are additions under new configurations or benchmarks, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The displayed waypoint and latent loss definitions change from sums in v1 Equations 4 and 7 to averages in v2 Equations 6 and 3. The view-selection reward formulation is removed, and perception-loss definitions are added. These are limited changes to mathematical definitions; neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes an annotation-free planner and acceleration through view selection. v2 replaces the acceleration contribution with applicability across perception-free and perception-based frameworks and extends its benchmark claim to NAVSIM. Its nuScenes discussion now describes the perception-free variant as competitive and attributes state-of-the-art performance to the perception-based variant.

C2.justification: v1's interpretations of view-selection saliency, front-view importance and computational savings disappear. v2 adds interpretations connecting NAVSIM compliance/progress gains to trajectory quality and richer perception to avoiding VAD's illustrated errors. It also identifies ineffective 10-second prediction as a boundary, while removing v1's explicit limited-data limitation and scalability discussion.

D1.justification: v2 documents NAVSIM hyperparameters, staged BEV training, deformable attention and appendix temporal-training schedules; stated nuScenes training hardware changes from eight RTX 3090s to eight A6000s. Selection fine-tuning and runtime-measurement details disappear. v2 also omits v1's explicit temporal-residual specification and two-block count, reducing detail for retained results. The repository link is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 expands its positioning through BERT and temporal predictive-coding references, contrasting earlier future prediction with action conditioning and image generation with direct latent prediction. Compatibility with perception-based systems becomes a central distinction. References also expand to NAVSIM/nuPlan, BEV-Planner, PARA-Drive and recent vision-language driving work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and methodology are extensively rewritten. The method now explains the world model before the two planner frameworks, replacing the earlier planner-first and view-selection organization. Experimental setup is split into benchmarks and implementation details, terminology changes from explicit/implicit to perception-based/perception-free, and the appendix is reorganized around different questions.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn, and the selection pipeline, selection plots and latency breakdown are replaced by LAW-versus-VAD visualizations. Tables gain framework groupings and NAVSIM metrics, lose latency/FPS columns, and combine the retained CARLA ablation with NAVSIM results. The conference template also changes typography and headers.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evidence that latent prediction works beyond v1's custom planner: the BEV ablations in Table 4 and NAVSIM ablation in Table 5 isolate its contribution in additional settings, while Appendix A.1 probes temporal extensions. These gains improve empirical support, but are moderated by weaker temporal-aggregation documentation for retained results and removal of the explicit data-scale limitation. The net improvement is meaningful but limited.
